corrections.what_happened: The row's retrieval and build_stats each held one sum without the model's name, a form the arms cannot share without adding two models together; build_stats counted 0 attempts for its calls.

rule.text:
1. A row's retrieval is its own call records summed per model (harness.capture.usage_by_model),
     the answer call left out. The answer call is the record whose system text is the harness's
     answer instruction; it is marked role: answer, and its tokens must be the generator's.
  2. The entries must hold what the row recorded: the same calls, tokens in, tokens out and cached
     tokens in all.
  3. artefact_v4 only: search_time_s loses the embedder's seconds (lock_wait_s + encode_s of the
     row's embed records) and the seconds of the first-call tries that did not answer (the chat
     entry's retry_s).
  4. build_stats gets one entry per model, from the run's own manifest: lucene none; vector the
     embedder, from its build_stats and the stored file's cost note; artefact_v4 from
     index.build_cost (artefact_v4.build_stats_from_cost).
  5. artefact_v4 only: the graph block takes the graph's last build record and the graph counted
     now (orchestrator.graph_census), after a check that the graph holds now what the run counted
     at its start.
  6. artefact_v4 only: the sha256 of the code files (meta.provenance.source_sha256) and of the
     build cost file (index.build_cost_file_sha256) become those of the commit's files, their
     line ends as git holds them (LF), after a check that each recorded value is the commit's
     file with the Windows line ends the checkout wrote.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: No answer, context, id, score or judge call is changed; the call records are changed only by the answer call's role.

A retrieval entry's seconds are the tries' and the embedder's own seconds from the call records. The sum the arm recorded held the seconds around each call, so the entries hold a little less; that rest is the arm's own work, in timing.wall_s.
timing.wall_s and the stamps are unchanged.

corrections.what_happened: The run embedded its queries on the CPU. Each question's query-embedding time is the time the same embeddings take on the desktop's GTX 1080 Ti.

rule.text:
1. The run embedded its queries on the CPU (every embed call record says device cpu).
  2. Each question's embed entry in retrieval gets request_s = the GPU seconds of its embed calls
     added, and time_s = request_s + wait_s + retry_s; wait_s and retry_s stay as recorded.
  3. The question's timing.wall_s changes by the same amount as the embed entry's request_s.
  4. Each embed call record gets its GPU seconds as encode_s and device cuda. No vector, answer,
     context, score or other time changes; the vectors are the same (cosine checked).

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: The GPU times were measured one call after the other in a warm process; the lock waits of the run (wait_s) stay as recorded.

evidence.what: per question, each embed call's GPU seconds and the cosine of its vector to the CPU one

corrections.what_happened: The two non-LLM context scores compared each gold record, written as its string values joined by spaces, with the texts handed over, written in HERB's own form, so the same record did not match itself.

before.what_it_did: each gold record as all of its string values joined by spaces, against the texts as handed over (eval/ragas.py at the commits that scored the three final runs on the hundred)

rule.text:
1. The evaluation compared gold records and handed-over texts in two forms that are not the
     same. The code that scored the three final runs on the hundred wrote each gold record as all
     of its string values joined by spaces, while every arm hands its records over in HERB's own
     form (harness.record_text), with ids, labels, dates and names around the content, so the
     same record did not match itself as a string. The code that scored the runs on the 715
     answerable questions wrote each gold record in record_text form, so the ids, labels, dates
     and names of the form were counted in how alike two records are.
  2. The artefact hands over chunks of several records; a whole chunk was compared with single
     gold records and never matched one.
  3. Both sides are reduced to record content (harness.record_content): each gold record's
     content, against the content of each record handed over, every text cut into its records
     (eval.ragas.contents_handed_over).
  4. context_recall_nonllm and context_precision_nonllm are calculated again by RAGAS's own
     NonLLMContextRecall and NonLLMContextPrecisionWithReference on those contents; every other
     score and every other file stays as it is.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: No answer, context, context_ids, other score or judge call is changed; arm_outputs.jsonl is as it was. The content is taken out only for these two scores; the answer model and the judge got the texts as they were handed over.
Content against content still counts different records as alike when their text is more than half the same, as HERB's templated Slack messages often are (output/research/2026-10-23-nonllm-checks).

checks.what: the questions file read here is the one the run read (its sha256 in the run manifest's inputs)
the corpus read here is the one the run read (its digest in the run manifest's inputs)
one method in BEFORE gives every stored score again (string-leaves)
every stored score was calculated again
every text is its records in record_text form, joined by a blank line (15643 texts handed over, 15610 records with content)
